lectures.label: A
lectures.title: Dental Endocrinology Clinical Application
lectures.note: Taught November 6 and moved here from Exam 2 (Dr. Herr left it off Exam 2), with everything the Exam 2 hub had for it.

likelyTopics.t: Hypoglycemia in the chair: the signs, a finger-stick (some CGMs stop reading at a floor), straight glucose rather than table sugar, a slow response on a GLP-1 drug, glucagon IM or subcutaneously if oral glucose fails

Before treating a diabetic: HbA1c above 7 is poorly controlled (implant failure, periodontal disease), confirm the meal and medication, morning appointments; Dr. Taylor's metformin with a skipped breakfast; pack-years
Hyperthyroidism and Graves disease (his first case): epinephrine caution, and thyroid storm (fever, pulse 140 or more; call 911)
Addison disease (his third case): oral pigment from high ACTH, adrenal crisis triggers and signs, extra corticosteroid after a big procedure; Cushing syndrome and long-term steroids
Hyperparathyroidism on the radiograph (lost lamina dura, radiolucent brown tumors, mobility) and the calcium regulators (PTH, vitamin D, calcitonin)
Acromegaly's growing jaw (Class I to Class III, diastemas, macroglossia); growth plates fused by the sex hormones, and implant timing
The three hormone classes with examples, receptors, and endocrine versus nervous signaling
Diabetes: type 1 versus type 2 (insulin ineffective, not deficient), oral manifestations and the sugar in saliva, the two-way periodontal link, SGLT2 drugs and UTIs
Hyperthyroid versus hypothyroid dental considerations (hypothyroidism far more common), and the recurrent laryngeal nerve in thyroid surgery
Sex hormones and the mouth: puberty, pregnancy gingivitis and the interproximal pyogenic granuloma, menopause
Pituitary hormones (ADH and diabetes insipidus), alpha and beta cells, and the adrenal medulla
